content: The selection of appropriate footwear, as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes the use of therapeutic footwear such as custom-made orthotic shoes. These types of footwear are specifically designed to help reduce plantar pressure and prevent the development of foot ulcers. It is advised to avoid wearing open-toed shoes, as they may increase the risk of injury or complications. Additionally, features such as rocker soles or metatarsal accommodations are beneficial as they help to redistribute pressure away from specific areas of the foot, thereby reducing localized stress and promoting foot health.
